title: Plate Tectonics
seo_title: Earth Sciences 11: Plate Tectonics Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
short_title: Earth's layers, plate boundaries and mantle convection
standard_text: Plate tectonic theory explains the distribution and formation of Earth's features: Earth's layers, evidence for plate tectonics, plate boundaries, mantle convection, and earthquakes and volcanoes. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Earth Sciences 11)
meta_desc: Free Earth Sciences 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): Earth's layers, plate boundaries and mantle convection. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth has a crust, mantle, outer core and inner core. The lithosphere is broken into plates that move on the softer asthenosphere, driven by mantle convection, ridge push and slab pull. Evidence includes matching continents and fossils, seafloor spreading, magnetic striping and the age of the ocean floor.

At divergent boundaries plates move apart (mid-ocean ridges); at convergent boundaries they collide (subduction zones, mountains); at transform boundaries they slide past (faults). The Cascadia subduction zone off BC can cause very large earthquakes.

Example

The seafloor is youngest at which feature?

New crust forms there.

Answer: the mid-ocean ridge

Example

What happens when oceanic crust meets continental crust?

Denser crust sinks.

Answer: the oceanic crust subducts

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the mantle is liquid.
  • Thinking continents move but the ocean floor does not.
  • Mixing up convergent and divergent boundaries.

faq.a: The Juan de Fuca plate subducts and melts beneath North America.
